outcome: sexual function (assessed using Female Sexual Function Index - FSFI)
cohort: 200 women who underwent either transobturator tape (TOT) or tension-free vaginal tape (TVT) procedures for stress urinary incontinence (SUI).
finding: Minimally invasive surgical procedures such as TOT and TVT not only effectively treat SUI but also may improve aspects of sexual function, particularly among nonmenopausal women and those with a history of natural delivery, with the TOT group generally showing better outcomes than TVT.
mod_finding: Women with a history of natural delivery in the TOT group demonstrated significantly higher sexual function compared to their counterparts in the TVT group, and similarly, women who had undergone cesarean delivery in the TOT group reported better sexual function than those in the TVT group.
